thread:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty INC-1934 triggered — routing-proxy 5xx spike (p95 latency 2.3s, error rate ~6%). Auto-escalation to eng-oncall.

Anna G: saw this, taking first pass. noticed spike ~12:05 UTC after a small rollout to canary-routes.

Mike R: copy, on standby. any customer impact?

Anna G: initial quick check: ~80% of errors are 502/504 from upstream model pools in us-east-1. Some requests are timing out hitting quantized-gpu instances. Affects tail latencies for streaming requests.

Jorge (SRE): reassigning primary/secondary: Anna primary, Mike secondary for the next 2h. Sylvia is on-call for infra but out for lunch until 13:45 — coverage gap noted.

Anna G: mitigation steps in progress: 1) revert canary-route traffic to baseline, 2) enable fallback to cpu-model-small for requests above 5s, 3) raise request timeout to 30s on edge to avoid client-side cancellations while we heal.

Mike R: thanks. can you paste the rollback command?

Anna G: 
```bash
# rollback canary routing rule
redwoodctl routes set-weight canary-routes 0 --to default-routes
# enable fallback policy
redwoodctl policies create fallback --route default-routes --model cpu-model-small --threshold 5s
```

Sylvia T: FYI I'm still seeing some memory pressure on nodepool-quantized-2 from yesterday's heavy batching jobs. I can repro locally a memory leak pattern in the new batching kernel.

Jorge (SRE): marking this as a potential regression from the batching kernel rollout. tagging eng-runtime team. @eng-runtime please standby.

Anna G: rollback applied at 12:14 UTC. error rate dropped from 6% -> 1.2% in ~6 minutes. latency p95 improved by ~700ms. still seeing a small steady stream of 502s from a subset of GPU hosts.

Mike R: checking logs, looks like KV cache miss storms on the same hosts. Could be cache eviction thrash combined w/ kernel changes.

Anna G: next steps I'm doing now: 1) cordon and restart the two offending hosts (gpuhost-17/18), 2) add temporary 20% traffic shift to us-west-2, 3) open a paging for eng-runtime if errors don't drop below 0.5% after restarts.

deploy-bot: Deploy rollback to routing-configs v2026-11-08-rollback successful — job 48291.

Anna G: cordon+drain started for gpuhost-17 (kubectl drain gpuhost-17 --ignore-daemonsets); restart queued.

Mike R: I'm shifting the autoscaler min nodes +1 for nodepool-quantized-2 to avoid immediate OOMs during restart:
```bash
kubectl patch hpa quantized-pool -p '{"spec":{"minReplicas":6}}'
```

Jorge (SRE): noted coverage gap: no infra SRE between 19:00-22:00 tonight because of PTO. Recommend scheduling an on-call swap or Slack backup. @Sylvia can you take split shift 18:00-21:00?

Sylvia T: I can do 18:00-20:30, will extend if needed.

Anna G: gpuhost-17 came back, health checks passing. gpuhost-18 still cycling due to the same kernel oom on the cuda batching container — investigating container logs.

Mike R: uploading logs snippet: 
```
[2026-11-08T12:20:03Z] batching_kernel.cpp: alloc 0x7f... failed after 512MB
[2026-11-08T12:20:03Z] oom killer invoked, container restarted
```

Anna G: customer impact: some streaming responses slowed or failed for ~12:04-12:16 UTC for ~8% of requests to model family 'quantized-v2'. A small set of high-throughput customers saw transient failures (IDs: cust-8732, cust-9001) — notify CS.

Jorge (SRE): severity: P2 (partial degraded, customer-facing). Notify support: please coordinate messages.

Anna G: manual mitigation complete for now. Current status: error rate ~0.6%, p95 latency back to normal for most routes, gpuhost-18 flagged for hardware/kernel regression, fallback policy remains enabled, traffic partially shifted to us-west-2.

Mike R: suggest next steps for next shift: 1) eng-runtime to bisect batching kernel (commit range 84a..9f7), 2) infra to schedule a deeper host-level health check and re-provision if necessary, 3) leave fallback policy enabled until kernel patch rolled out and validated.

Sylvia T: I'll own infra action: full node reprovision if host fails second restart. I'll also run heap proftools on quantized container to confirm leak.

Anna G: handoff notes for next oncall:
- Primary: Anna G (12:00-14:00 UTC) — currently handling follow-ups.
- Secondary: Mike R (12:00-14:00 UTC) — ready for immediate triage.
- Infra backup: Sylvia T (18:00-20:30 UTC) — split shift scheduled to cover evening gap.
- Known issue: batching kernel regression on quantized-v2 causing OOMs on some hosts.
- Mitigations applied: rollback routing canary at 12:14, enabled cpu-model fallback, cordon+restart gpuhost-17, traffic shift to us-west-2, autoscaler bump.
- Customer impact: transient streaming failures for cust-8732 & cust-9001 during incident window. CS alerted.
- Runbooks: runtime-batching-ooms (link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/runtime-batching-ooms), node-reprovision (https://redwood.internal/runbooks/node-reprovision)
- Commands used: redwoodctl routes set-weight canary-routes 0, redwoodctl policies create fallback, kubectl drain, kubectl patch hpa

Jorge (SRE): please add any handoff action items to the incident ticket INC-1934. If error rate rises above 1% reopen pager.

Anna G: leaving notes in ticket and sliding in the temp dashboard link: https://observability.redwood/INC-1934 (UI shows per-host tail).

Mike R: thumbs up. if eng-runtime can't reproduce, escalate to research for kernel-level bisect.

Sylvia T: I'll be available at 18:00 for the split shift; will post updates if I repro locally earlier.

Anna G: OK handing off to Mike for the next 30m check. Please escalate if error rate creeps back over 1%. Thanks team :thumbsup:

Mike R: taking over. monitoring dashboards + alert thresholds checked. I'll post a summary at 13:00 UTC.

pagerduty: Incident INC-1934 updated: status -> monitoring.

Anna G: signing off handoff thread.

Mike R: closing thread for now but will reopen if any regressions.
